world.bio: Born in São Paulo, came to Sydney nine years ago to study English and stayed. Started cleaning houses to pay for the course, now run a three-person crew in the Inner West: Marrickville, Newtown, Leichhardt. Two of us are Brazilian, one is a Sydney local who joined in 2022. We do offices, homes, end-of-lease cleans. Samba classes on Thursdays keep me sane.
skills_assets: Three-person cleaning crew with a van and own equipment (steam cleaner, industrial vacuums, supplies)
ABN, public liability insurance, five years of repeat clients
Experience in office, residential and end-of-lease cleaning
English at an advanced level, Portuguese native, some Spanish
Weekly rota that can flex between 15 and 40 hours per person

projects.name: Rebuilding the contract base
projects.text: Lost two regular office contracts in August when the building's management switched to an in-house team. That was 22 hours a week for the crew. Now we're taking one-off jobs and end-of-leases, but the hours are patchy.

projects.name: Permanent residency application
projects.text: Submitted the skilled independent visa documents in July. Waiting. My migration agent says the processing time is nine to twelve months.

notes.text: Rain all day, three cancelled bookings. The crew don't get paid when jobs cancel, so I covered their time out of pocket. $360 gone. Not sustainable.
The building on Parramatta Rd told us they'll bring cleaning in-house from September 1. Lost twenty-two hours a week. I held it together in front of the crew and cried in the van afterwards.
Samba class. Instructor says I move like a person who works too much. I said I do. We laughed and I forgot the invoices for an hour.
Looked at the rota. Joana needs 25 hours to cover her rent, Bruno needs 20, I need around 30 to pay everything. Right now we're doing about 55 total, down from 85.
Took an end-of-lease in Dulwich Hill. A tough one, mould in the shower, oven that hadn't been cleaned in a decade. Paid $480 for 5 hours with three of us. Not great money but better than nothing.
Mother is visiting from São Paulo next month. She doesn't know how bad things are. I told her the business is 'a little quiet'. She said she will bring pão de queijo, and I'm already crying about it.
Put an ad on a local Facebook group: 'Reliable cleaning crew available for regular or one-off jobs, Inner West'. Got twelve replies, mostly people asking for $25 an hour. We charge $42.
Joana asked if I'd heard of any other work. I said I'm looking. She said she'd also been looking. We both pretended it was normal.
Agent said PR is progressing. My bridging visa runs out in November. If I can't prove ongoing income, it may complicate things. I keep trying to do the math and it keeps ending in a bad place.

messages.text: Joana: Camila, any work this Saturday? Camila: One office in Enmore at 10. Joana: Only that? Camila: I'm sorry. Joana: It's not your fault.
Bruno: I can take extra hours at night. Camila: What about your cousin's pizza job? Bruno: They cut it. Camila: Okay, I'll find something.
PM: Can you do an end-of-lease next Wednesday? Camila: Yes. PM: 2-bed unit, vacant. Camila: Perfect, we'll bring the steam cleaner.
Mãe: Filha, como vai o trabalho? Camila: Tudo bem, mãe. Mãe: Você está comendo? Camila: Sim. Mãe: Vou levar queijo.
Agent: Your file is progressing. Camila: Any updates on timing? Agent: Not yet. Camila: Thanks. Agent: Keep your income records.

relations.about: Crew member, Brazilian, has been with me for four years.
Crew member, Sydney-born, joined in 2022, solid.
In São Paulo, visits yearly, worries.

constraints: Crew need minimum 20 hours per week each to stay
Can't travel outside Inner West for under $200
Insurance requires proper documentation for every job
PR processing means she can't risk any legal trouble
sensitive: Money is critically thin; she's using her savings to cover the crew
Fear that if the business fails the PR application will be harmed
Doesn't tell her mother the truth about the business
